note: Design data, not shipped content. An Activity type is individuated by shown x produced x withheld. Feedback timing, scoring rule, provenance and Condition-axis settings are parameters, not types. Widget is not here at all - it is LDB-07's.

poolRule.statement: A supplied pool is cosmetic when it discloses any part of what is being measured; substantive when the measured target is not in the pool.

rules.case: word bank over 'which hands would you double'
fragment assembly where the target is the order
rules.why: the pool supplies elements; the order is not in it
the grid supplies the space, not the actions
not a supplied pool - a real table enumerates the action space too

poolRule.overturns: U2/audit.md:80's generation-from-scratch test, which that row itself records as a borderline rejection half-decided by dispatch scope.
poolRule.disagreesWith: classification.md's cosmetic call on U3-7, which is reclassified substantive here and disposed of on a different ground (no target).

recognitionRule.statement: An activity measures by recognition when the prompt assembles candidate answers for that item, or supplies a Classification the learner should have made. Displaying the invariant action set is not recognition.
recognitionRule.consequence: strategy-action, legal-fallback and adherence-under-loss are all classificationIncluded:true, so their prompts may never name the hand shape, so they must show cards, so those cards must have come from a shoe. All three are unmeasurable without dealt hands.
recognitionRule.notRequired: Withholding the action set to force production. Roediger et al. (U3/audit.md:18): production scored 6-7% lower on matched items, and on the delayed exam tested 70% vs nontested 73%, 'opposite the predicted direction', F=1.50.

provenance.recordedAs: read off existing card ids - 'deck-N-...' is organic, 'arranged-N-...' is arranged, no cards at all is posed
provenance.mechanism: crates/blackjack-core/src/shoe.rs:62 create_prefix_shoe - each arranged card replaces a shuffled card of the same rank and suit, so composition is unchanged and the arrangement labels itself
provenance.ruling: Arranged is dealt evidence for the Skill. Whether arranged-only evidence can reach mastery is LDB-04's to rule; see A-23.

coverageRule.forward: every Activity type declares at least one Skill it measures, OR declares a non-empty rehearses
coverageRule.reverse: every Skill names at least one Activity type that could produce primary evidence for it
coverageRule.onGap: a Skill no type can cover is recorded as a finding against LDB-01 - never filled by inventing an activity
coverageRule.result: 18 of 18 Skills covered by primary evidence; 11 of 11 types declare coverage or rehearsal

ungradedAdmission.clause: An Activity type may grade nothing PROVIDED it declares rehearses - a non-empty list of Skill ids it gives practice at without producing evidence for.
ungradedAdmission.rehearsalIsNotCoverage: rehearses NEVER contributes to the reverse direction. A Skill named only in a rehearses list is still uncovered, and onGap still applies to it.
ungradedAdmission.notABudget: No fixed count of ungraded types. A fixed budget was offered to the owner and refused as a constant with nothing behind it.
citedNotReargued: LDB-04 D6: 'not everything the learner does needs to feed a progress meter. An app in which every interaction is graded is a quiz with a card table drawn behind it'
A-18's validation method: 'instrument the first non-quiz activity against a quiz baseline' - unclosable until these types existed

activityTypes.title: Deal and decide
activityTypes.shown: a Decision situation as dealt cards plus the dealer upcard, under a named ruleset
activityTypes.produced: the Classification (pair / soft / hard) when the target Skill has classificationIncluded:true, then one action from the legal set
activityTypes.withheld: the Classification, the correct action, and the hand outcome

parameters.note: the EV-graded form is foreclosed - LDB-01 gives EV no Skill and the oracle returns an action, not a number
realises the existing support Condition axis; rungs are A-04
realises the existing pace Condition axis; A-02
record which resources the learner actually opened - product-design-inputs 4.5

activityTypes.note: classify-hand is carried here as a separately graded sub-response, not as its own Activity type. P2 Bottom line A.2: classification should be measured separately from action selection (discrimination errors 46% vs 10%; 72% vs 38%, d=1.05).

activityTypes.title: State report
activityTypes.shown: a dealt hand, a round in progress, or a resolved hand and its wager - always as real cards
activityTypes.produced: the stated value, total, predicate, settlement, or bankroll change
activityTypes.withheld: the value itself, and for natural-blackjack the Classification
activityTypes.note: natural-blackjack is classificationIncluded:true, so its prompt may not say 'this is a natural' - it must show the two cards and let the learner name it.

activityTypes.title: Policy paint
activityTypes.shown: the strategy space - either as a grid of Decision situations, or withheld entirely so the learner must generate the region too
activityTypes.produced: an action for every situation in the region - a complete policy, not a cell
activityTypes.classificationSuppliedNote: In the presented-grid setting the grid is organised by pair / soft / hard, which hands the learner the Classification. Evidence from this type therefore covers the action-selection half of strategy-action only. The withheld setting does not supply it. LDB-04 rules whether classification-supplied evidence can reach mastery.

parameters.note: presented-grid supplies the Classification; withheld does not, and is the setting that satisfies classificationIncluded:true

activityTypes.note: Adopted from U1-1. classification.md: decomposing a policy into per-cell items destroys the measurement, because presenting the cell supplies the recall. This is also why LDB-01's 'a cellId is not a licence to drill cells as items' is not violated here - the response object is the policy.

activityTypes.title: Rule card read
activityTypes.shown: an active table and its behaviour, with the rule card itself withheld
activityTypes.produced: the table's dealer soft-17 rule, deck count, double-after-split rule, and blackjack payout

parameters.note: the shown-mid-session setting is U3-5's dynamic assessment - present the resource and measure whether the learner applies it

activityTypes.title: Predict then reveal
activityTypes.shown: a named event and a stated number of upcoming hands, before they are played
activityTypes.produced: one frequency - how often the learner expects the event to occur
activityTypes.withheld: the outcome; the hands have not been played yet

parameters.note: inherits A-07. Constraint carried from the source: 'single items are near-useless' - the signal must aggregate across many predictions before any threshold is read off it
the sandbox is the reveal half only. product-design-inputs 4.4: a simulation that does not first capture a prediction is decoration

activityTypes.note: PRODUCED is one number because the approved Learning outcome says 'states how often they expect the event to occur'. U1-3's two-bound interval would have amended an outcome approved 2026-08-01.

activityTypes.title: Rule contrast
activityTypes.shown: the same Decision situations resolved under two different rulesets, side by side
activityTypes.produced: which of the table's rules differs between them
activityTypes.withheld: the rule, and any surfaced verdict on the learner's answer

parameters.note: recorded, never shown as pass/fail - U1-5's surviving licence

U2-6 inverted: show a decision that must flip, ask which rule flips it. PRODUCED is the same object - the rule - so this is a shown parameter, not a new type. verdictSurfaced:false governs both settings.

activityTypes.divergesFromSource: U3-4's construct is invention whose value is orthogonal to answer correctness - 'the students in the inventing condition did not generate a correct standardizing procedure during instruction, yet they were more prepared to learn the procedure.' This design grades the named differing rule so the activity produces evidence at all, and keeps the source's caution by not surfacing the verdict. Labelled Product judgement; the divergence is real and recorded rather than smoothed.
activityTypes.note: Its downstream evidence is the deal-and-decide attempts that follow under ruleset: novel-profile.

activityTypes.title: Hand sort
activityTypes.shown: a batch of dealt hands, all at once
activityTypes.produced: a partition of the batch into pair / soft / hard
activityTypes.withheld: which bucket each hand belongs in
activityTypes.adoptedFrom: U2-10 is elsewhere; this is U2-7
activityTypes.note: LDB-03 rejected U2-7 because classify-hand already has primary evidence in situ inside deal-and-decide - a MEASUREMENT argument that does not bite once the activity measures nothing. Kinetic, fast and forgiving; the most Duolingo-shaped interaction in the catalog. Cheapest instrument for A-18.

activityTypes.title: Estimate and check
activityTypes.shown: either a standing quantity about the game (how often a dealer showing 6 busts) or a live shoe position (from here, how often does hitting win)
activityTypes.withheld: the true value, which already exists and is computable
activityTypes.mergeReason: U1-2 and U2-4 differ only in shown. produced (a number) and withheld (the true value) are identical, and the individuating axis is shown x produced x withheld - so they are one type with a subject parameter, not two types.
activityTypes.distinctFrom: predict-then-reveal, whose withheld is 'the outcome; the hands have not been played yet'. That is a forecast whose evidence does not exist at capture time; this is a check against a value already determined. A-13 already carries the this-shoe-from-here half, whose whole point is scoring against the computed value and never against what the shoe did.
activityTypes.note: The shoe-position setting is scored against the engine's computed value and NEVER against what the shoe actually did - that is the decision/outcome separation the product exists to teach.

activityTypes.title: Procedure order
activityTypes.shown: the steps of a fixed procedure, scrambled, possibly with distractors to leave unused
activityTypes.produced: the steps in their correct order

parameters.note: lookup-sequence is classify -> dealer column -> cell

activityTypes.doesNotReinstate: round-flow. That Skill was retired because 'follow' names no observable act. This type creates NO Skill and produces no evidence; ordering is an observable act that here measures nothing. Recorded because the resemblance is close enough to look like a retired Skill returning by the back door.
activityTypes.note: LDB-03 reclassified U3-7 substantive under the pool ruling - the pool supplies fragments, the target is the order, and the two do not intersect - then did not adopt it because no Skill in the approved graph is an ordering. That remains true; this type does not change it.

activityTypes.title: Principle name
activityTypes.shown: several Decision situations presented as a group, all taking the same action
activityTypes.withheld: the shared action, and the reason they are alike
activityTypes.classificationSuppliedNote: Grouping the situations tells the learner they are the same kind, which supplies the Classification. That is exactly why LDB-03 rejected U3-9 under the recognition rule - and it is harmless here ONLY because this type produces no evidence for any classificationIncluded:true Skill. If it ever became graded, the recognition ban would bite immediately.
activityTypes.note: Rehearses strategy-action at the REGION level rather than the cell level - the pattern-spotting pleasure, which is a different pleasure from recall-or-decide. Its source is the weakest-evidenced substantive row in the catalog (N=20, one experiment, no replication, contrived by its own authors), which is why A-26 exists and why this is the first of the five to playtest.

activityTypes.title: Rule battery
activityTypes.shown: a set of fixed parts from which a policy rule can be assembled
activityTypes.produced: a rule, then a run of it against generated hands
activityTypes.withheld: the cells where the rule breaks

parameters.note: fixed-parts ONLY. The free-text form needs a rule language and a parser and stays rejected.

activityTypes.costCorrection: LDB-03 rejected U2-10 partly as needing 'a rule language and a parser'. That costed the FREE-TEXT form. Fixed-part assembly yields a rule object directly and the battery is the existing oracle evaluated over enumerated situations, so the admitted form needs neither. The cheap form was not costed because nobody asked for it.
activityTypes.note: The only type in the set with a builder shape rather than a recall-or-decide shape, and the one that most changes what the product is. Surfaces a wrong MODEL rather than a wrong answer - which is what the U2-14 decline gives up, and this is its named replacement.

patternVerdicts.name: Whole-policy range painting (169 cells)
patternVerdicts.reason: The response object is a complete policy over a space the prompt does not mark. classification.md: decomposing it into per-cell items destroys the measurement.

patternVerdicts.name: Pastcasting behind an information cut-off
patternVerdicts.reason: Substantive, but retrospective. variance-expectation is prospective by its approved outcome - 'before they are played'. No Skill in the graph is retrospective forecasting.

patternVerdicts.name: Two-bound interval elicitation, hit-rate scored
patternVerdicts.reason: The approved Learning outcome states a frequency, not bounds, so adopting it would amend a spec approved 2026-08-01. Provenance is vendor-self-description and the audit withdrew its corroboration claim on 2026-07-26. The source concedes the score is gamed by widening - slide 11: high scorers 'are simply willing to use wider ranges. Generally about 2 to 10 times wider.'

patternVerdicts.name: Open-ended information gathering before hypothesis
patternVerdicts.reason: Its core idea - score what the learner consulted separately from the answer - becomes an honest-assistance recording obligation on every type, per product-design-inputs 4.5.

patternVerdicts.name: LOFT uninterrupted run, judgement deferred to debrief
patternVerdicts.reason: Evidence-backed and independent on its own row label, discounted only for resting on one compilation. The deferral is a timing setting, not a question shape - the prompt is unchanged, which classification.md says outright.

patternVerdicts.name: Post-hoc graded decision-quality session review
patternVerdicts.reason: The binary form is a scoring setting on the deferred debrief. The catalogued EV-graded form is foreclosed: LDB-01 gives EV no Skill, and strategy.rs is a lookup returning an action with zero matches for expected_value across the crate.

patternVerdicts.name: Key-features critical-step-only case, write-in half
patternVerdicts.reason: Conditional resolved. Reducing a shoe to its 2-5 critical decisions requires telling the learner which decisions are critical - which supplies exactly the discrimination the recognition rule says the stimulus must not supply.

patternVerdicts.name: SPOT interruptible single-objective segment drill
patternVerdicts.reason: Segmenting a shoe and repeating until clean changes how much is attempted, not what is asked.

patternVerdicts.name: LOE event-set scoring, criteria fixed in advance
patternVerdicts.reason: Publishing the criteria before the run is a scoring policy over an unchanged prompt. It is also the concrete form of U1-5's surviving licence - issue no pass/fail verdict, but do not grade nothing.

patternVerdicts.name: Free-typed transcription of an audio stimulus
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic - a widget over an unchanged stimulus.

patternVerdicts.name: Spoken production scored by speech recognition
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic - classification.md's own words, 'a channel swap over an unchanged target'. The response deadline that would make it substantive is separable from the microphone, and is adopted separately as the pace parameter.

patternVerdicts.name: Stroke tracing on a touch surface
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic as sourced. Its substantive reading comes from the candidate-analogue column, which the archive warns over-rates this row. The blank-grid analogue it points at is already registered as A-21 and is adopted through policy-paint instead.

patternVerdicts.name: Continuous placement on a number line
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic - a continuous widget over a question a selection widget asks equally well.

patternVerdicts.name: Free-form sketch before formal representation
patternVerdicts.reason: Substantive, but its blackjack use - sketch the bust-rate curve before the chart is revealed - produces a curve. The only distributional Skill in the graph produces a frequency. Same ground as U1-3, without U1-3's provenance problems: hold it for a graph that has a curve-shaped outcome.

patternVerdicts.name: Construct-an-object-to-hit-a-target
patternVerdicts.reason: Its blackjack form is the inverse chart cell - give the action, ask which situation produces it. That is cell drilling under a different label, which LDB-01 forecloses: a cellId records where evidence came from and is not a licence to drill cells as items.

patternVerdicts.name: Multi-item categorisation (card sort)
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic as sourced. classify-hand already has primary evidence in situ as a graded sub-response of deal-and-decide, which is what P2 Bottom line A.2 asks for - measured separately, not measured elsewhere.

patternVerdicts.name: Semantically graded symbolic / numeric entry
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic - a grading tolerance over an unchanged question.

patternVerdicts.name: Typed free recall + learner self-rating
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic on the typing half, and the self-rating half is affirmatively contradicted by evidence this project already holds: Kornell and Bjork, 78% performed better spaced while 78% rated massed as good or better. The learner does not know what worked. This is the strongest rejection in the set.

patternVerdicts.name: Author an artifact judged by a test suite
patternVerdicts.reason: It measures the same thing policy-paint measures - a complete policy over an unpresented space - and needs a rule language and a parser to do it. Two instruments for one Skill; the cheaper one is already adopted. Buildability tier recorded, not the reason.

patternVerdicts.name: Continuous timed stream, per-element statistics
patternVerdicts.reason: Conditional resolved substantive - the blackjack analogue is externally paced, and external pacing is what the determinant asks for. But per-element statistics over a counting stream needs a counting Skill, and none exists. This is card counting's natural home; the graph already anticipates it as a fifth Condition axis.

patternVerdicts.name: Real-time performance on an external instrument
patternVerdicts.reason: Dealing on a fixed clock rather than on response realises the pace Condition axis the graph already declares. Note this row alone carries compensated-third-party provenance.

patternVerdicts.name: Simulation-configuration puzzle
patternVerdicts.reason: Adopted as the reveal half of predict-then-reveal only. product-design-inputs 4.4 is explicit that a simulation which does not first capture a prediction is decoration, and A-22 already registers the unevidenced teaching claim.

patternVerdicts.name: Free-composition typed answer to an open prompt
patternVerdicts.reason: Graded, it needs language understanding this project has no reason to build. Ungraded, it produces no evidence. And there is no Skill left for it either way: LDB-01 dropped the 'explain' half of every compound Skill under 1.7, measure play not quiz scores.

patternVerdicts.name: Unaided free recall ('write down everything')
patternVerdicts.reason: Free recall over a region is policy-paint with the grid taken away. That matters beyond economy: the presented grid is organised by pair / soft / hard and so supplies the Classification, and this setting is the one that does not. Evidence-backed, independent, in the catalog's six-row base.

patternVerdicts.name: Short-answer test with a lesson-wide word bank
patternVerdicts.reason: Cosmetic under the measurement-target test - the bank contains the answers, so it discloses part of the target. This card's ruling agrees with classification.md here.

patternVerdicts.name: Guidance-faded worked example / completion problem
patternVerdicts.reason: This is Seed B, and it realises the support Condition axis that LDB-01 made primary on the owner's 2026-07-23 decision. The principle is evidence-backed; the specific rungs are A-04.

patternVerdicts.name: Contrasting-cases invention task
patternVerdicts.reason: Two rulesets side by side, learner infers the rule that explains the difference. Rulesets are already parameterised in the engine. Divergence from the source recorded on the type: this design grades the named rule so the activity produces evidence, and keeps the source's caution by not surfacing a verdict.

patternVerdicts.name: Dynamic assessment with an embedded learning resource
patternVerdicts.reason: The strongest substantive case in the catalog on its own source's words - 'the two forms of instruction would have looked the same had we not included the resource item from which students could learn.' Present the rule card mid-session and measure whether the learner applies it.

patternVerdicts.name: Construct-a-concept-map, learner-created phrases
patternVerdicts.reason: No Skill in the graph is a proposition network, and the row's own evidence runs against its headline: the freer widget performed worse against the external criterion, r = .243 n.s. vs .551 p<.05, interrater 0.81 vs 0.92. Rejected rather than held open, because both the target and the merits are against it.

patternVerdicts.name: Fragment-assembly ordering (Parsons-style)
patternVerdicts.reason: Reclassified substantive by this card's pool ruling - the pool supplies fragments and distractors, the target is the order, and the two do not intersect. This overturns classification.md's cosmetic call. It is then not adopted for an unrelated reason: LDB-01 retired round-flow and complete-round, so no Skill in the approved graph is an ordering. The boundary is ruled and has nothing to attach to.

patternVerdicts.name: Continuous probability estimate, proper scoring rule
patternVerdicts.reason: Independent and Evidence-backed, and its response shape matches the approved Learning outcome verbatim. Its own recorded weakness - 'single items are near-useless' - is a threshold problem, which is LDB-04's and which the graph already flags as inheriting A-07.

patternVerdicts.name: Convergent-cue generation (one answer, six cues)
patternVerdicts.reason: Presenting five situations as a group that share an action tells the learner they are the same kind - supplying the Classification for a classificationIncluded:true Skill, which the recognition rule forbids. Independently, it is the weakest-evidenced substantive row in the catalog: N=20, one experiment, no replication, measuring later memory rather than abstraction, and its own authors call it contrived.

playVerdicts.question: Would this be good to PLAY, accepting that it measures nothing? A question none of these rows was asked when it was disposed.
playVerdicts.whyItIsNewRatherThanARerun: classification.md's classifier was told 'not to rank on usefulness to the product, and not to invent a composite score'. Its only axis is substantive-vs-cosmetic on MEASUREMENT. The 19 rows below were disposed on whether they measure something this product needs measured.
playVerdicts.scope: Exactly the 19 rows LDB-03 disposed as rejected (15) or not-adopted-no-target (4). The original measurement verdicts are NOT altered - this is a second, independent axis.
playVerdicts.quotationProvenance: Where a reason quotes a source, the quotation is reproduced from the catalog row and was NOT re-verified at source. The card forbade new collection. Stated plainly rather than implied.

verdicts.reason: Dragging cards into buckets is kinetic, fast and forgiving - the most Duolingo-shaped interaction in the catalog. The measurement objection (classify-hand is already measured in situ) does not bite on an activity that measures nothing.

Replaying a resolved hand and asking for a probability, scored against the engine and never against what the shoe did, is decision/outcome separation made visceral - the misconception the product exists to defeat. Merged with U2-4; see the type's mergeReason.

Sliding a guess at the dealer-6 bust rate and watching the true value snap in is a low-friction curiosity beat, and it delivers how-to-teach.md Part 4's 'teach bust rates BEFORE showing the chart'. Merged with U1-2.

Ordering is a great play shape - tactile, fast, forgiving - and the natural 'how does this game work' onboarding beat. Not adopted for measurement because no Skill is an ordering; that is still true and this type does not change it.

Pattern-spotting is a different pleasure from recall-or-decide, and it is the only row in the set that offers it. The recognition-rule objection dissolves once nothing is measured. Its teaching claim is thin and is filed as A-26.

Authoring a rule and watching it tested is a builder fantasy and the most distinctive thing in the catalog. The rejection was measurement economy - 'two instruments for one Skill' - which says nothing about play. See the type's costCorrection: the admitted form needs no parser.

A genuine puzzle, and the only 'aha' shape in the set. The cell-drilling objection misses that the play object is the RULE, not the cell. Same produced object as rule-contrast, so a parameter rather than a type.

Good to play - drawing the frontier is tactile and matches how the strategy is actually held, as a shape rather than 169 facts. But it is a WIDGET over policy-paint, and the scope fence puts widget in LDB-07. A-21 already registers the claim; carry the verdict, do not re-derive it.

Genuinely good to play - the arcade beat, and counting is what casual players find glamorous. Needs the counting Skill that phase 7's fifth Condition axis introduces. Recorded positively so phase 7 inherits the verdict.

Gameable by widening - its own source concedes high scorers 'are simply willing to use wider ranges. Generally about 2 to 10 times wider.' A game whose winning move is to answer vaguely is a bad game, and predict-then-reveal already occupies the calibration slot.

Reducing a shoe to its 2-5 critical decisions requires telling the learner which decisions are critical. That kills the play for the same reason it killed the measurement: the interesting part was noticing.
Typing where tapping is equal. Friction with no payoff.

Saying the play aloud is genuinely table-like and the most tempting decline here. It needs a microphone and speech recognition, and it excludes accented speakers, non-English speakers and anyone in a public place. The pressure half is separable and already adopted as pace.

The freehand curve is the fiddly, feel-bad form of estimate-and-check; drawing badly feels like failing. Ten repeated point estimates build the same curve and each one feels like a guess worth making.
Typing a number where tapping is equal. Friction. The true-count and bet-unit entries it names become live only with phase 7's counting.

The self-rating half is contradicted by evidence this project already holds - Kornell and Bjork, 78% performed better spaced while 78% rated massed as good or better. It is also a mood-killer. Declined on both counts, as it was rejected on both.

Free-text 'explain the play' reads as homework, and an open box most players skip is worse than no box. What dies with it is the catalog's only route to surfacing a MISCONCEPTION rather than a wrong answer - replaced by rule-battery and the which-rule-would-flip-this probe, which surface wrong models at no typing cost.
The word bank contains the answers, so there is no decision left to make. A puzzle with its solution printed beside it is not a puzzle.

Concept mapping is a school assignment, not a game - and its own evidence runs against its headline widget (r = .243 n.s. vs .551 p<.05; interrater 0.81 vs 0.92). The causal chain it points at is delivered as play by estimate-and-check instead.

playVerdicts.removalNamesItsReplacement: AGENTS.md Constraints. The only decline that gives up a capability nothing else carries is U2-14 (surfacing a misconception rather than a wrong answer). Its replacement is named on its row and is real: rule-battery and rule-contrast.probe both surface wrong models.

proceduralRulesApplied: Classified from the sourced pattern, never the candidate-analogue column - U2-3, U2-11 and U2-13 over-rate on that column.
Used each row's own provenance label, not its unit's - U1-5, U1-8 and U1-9 are Evidence-backed and independent, so 'vendor self-description' would have been a false reason for them.
Buildability tier recorded where relevant, never used as a reason - that file is self-declared Product judgement and converges on the standing phase-5 candidate by the same author.

checkedAndAlreadyPresent: A-21 covers U2-3's blank-grid analogue, which policy-paint adopts and LDB-09 forwards to LDB-07
A-22 covers U2-13's variance sandbox, which predict-then-reveal adopts as its reveal half
A-13 covers estimate-and-check's this-shoe-from-here half - training decision evaluation independently of the hand result
A-18 is the CLASS premise for every ungraded type, and LDB-09 makes it closable: its method needed a first non-quiz activity, and five now exist
checkedAndDoesNotStretch: A-22 covers a CONFIGURABLE SANDBOX the learner sets up and runs. That is not point-estimate elicitation, which is why estimate-and-check gets A-27 rather than riding A-22. Checked rather than assumed.
registerDelta.notReissued: A-25 - allocated to a cap dropped at LDB-05 and recorded in the register as never filed. LDB-09's rows are A-26 to A-28 so that record stays readable.
